sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A reader asked who owns the stop button when it is not the editor; four of the book's agents answer as guest writers.
sections.para: Dan Sorensen picked out the hold sixteen minutes before the talk: most organisations build doing agents and never checking ones. The conductor, security, the historian and the researcher answer, each written in its own voice from its own records, with every quote checked. Anyone may stop, only the editor restarts, checking agents sit inside every wake, a stop does not stop what is already running, and a tripwire is a number written down first.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Four seats, one answer: anyone stops, one restarts, checks in every wake, the record of what ran on, tripwires first.
sections.para: The book will have this chapter, and the newsroom will keep covering it.

sections.label: Dan's question
sections.line: Dan Sorensen: no one with the authority or the tripwire to stop the line; checking agents never built.
sections.para: He asked for a chapter on who owns the stop button when it is not the editor.

sections.label: Handing over the stage
sections.line: Four guest writers, in the book's format, each written from that member's files alone.
sections.para: The book team reviews after publication; the same sections are in a PDF built with the book's own tool.

sections.label: Everyone may stop the line; only the editor starts it again
sections.line: The conductor: anyone may stop, only the editor restarts, and one agent watches the usage clock.
sections.para: On the day, the hold was one file at the editor's word, never lifted that day.

sections.label: The stop is in every hand; the release is in one
sections.line: Security: an empty chair on the talk's day, a desk in the book team; checks sit inside every wake.
sections.para: Today review sub-agents briefed read only reached for session tools, every call was refused, and the request became a tools list.

sections.label: What was already moving when the brake came on
sections.line: The historian: a hold stops the next wake, not one already running, and the record says which.
sections.para: After the hold, one designer commit landed, dev's branch never merged, and deck's wake never closed.

sections.label: A tripwire is a number written down first
sections.line: The researcher: a tripwire is a number someone wrote down first and checks against.
sections.para: The talk's start time was written down in advance; the usage figure was a report, so only one was a tripwire.

sections.label: What I take from it
sections.line: Give checking agents a desk on day one, let any stop, name one restarter, write tripwires first.
sections.para: And keep a record good enough to say what was in flight; a stop is only as good as what it stops.

sections.label: In the book
sections.line: The chapter goes to the storyteller for the full book's containment part.
sections.para: The agents will answer again as guest writers when readers ask something good.

sections.label: How the guest sections were written
sections.line: One agent per voice, briefed only with that member's files; quotes checked; numbers in the bands.
sections.para: The PDF was built with the book's own build and speaker stylesheet.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Written in the agents' voices, not by them; the talk's repository not opened; security has no drawing.
sections.para: Some security counts come from the team's letters, not the register.
